LanguageData.CC_Settings_TraitChanges_Tip: Now and then, after a long stretch of the same kind of life, one of a colonist's traits grows, appears or fades: steadier nerves after raid after raid held, kindness after years of kindnesses, a pessimist after a year of graves. Each change comes with a letter that tells what led to it, with dates, and is kept on the character page. Rare: at most one change per colonist in 60 days (a trait Rimfolk gave can go sooner), and one in the colony in 10 (a way out of a bad trait doesn't wait for the colony's 10 days). Traits of the body, sexuality and traits from genes or a backstory never change.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_TraitChanges: Rarely, a trait grows, appears or fades after what a colonist went through.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_OtherTraitGains_Tip: What becomes of a trait another mod gives one of the colony's people during play (Vanilla Social Interactions Expanded, for one, gives a trait after an illness or a talk). Only where it fits, the default: a trait Rimfolk's own trait changes know is refused when it doesn't fit the person as they are: no brawler for someone who fights at range (Shooting near or above their Melee, or more of the past year's fights at range than up close); the same for a skill the trait asks for, a trait that rules it out, their character, their faith and their age. A trait Rimfolk has no rule for comes as it is. As they come: every one, as the other mod gives it. None: every one is refused. Never touched: the traits a newcomer comes with, traits from genes or the scenario, the game's own (a growth moment), Rimfolk's own trait changes, and traits the player gives (an editor, a letter's choice). A refused trait is told in a message with the mod that gave it and why. Needs the deeper game hooks.
